name: Liveland Raspberry

origin.place: Livonia (Livland Governorate of the Russian Empire, now Latvia/Estonia)

history: A Baltic apple from the old Livland province, recorded before 1870 and among the 'Russian' apples imported to the American Midwest (credited to A. G. Tuttle of Baraboo, Wisconsin); it was formally introduced in the US in 1883. It is often linked to the ancestry of Melba and is a parent of Joyce.

look.description: Waxy, pale cream apple flushed and striped light crimson; the white flesh is often stained pinkish red.

taste.summary: Fine, very tender white flesh tinged red, mildly sweet with gentle acidity and a light perfume. Unusually for a summer apple it stays pleasant on and off the tree for a short while.

tree.notes: Naturally small, upright and compact tree even on its own roots; inclined to crop every other year.

pollination.notes: National Fruit Collection blossom dates are early mid-season (about group 2-3).

climate.best_climates: Cold continental and northern climates: the Baltic, Scandinavia, the upper Midwest and New England, where its winter-hardiness matters.
climate.poor_climates: Hot summers ripen summer apples like this too fast and soften them; it has little advantage in mild climates.

health.other: Biennial bearing is the main recorded fault.

grow_notes: A compact, very hardy early apple for cold gardens. Thin the fruit in heavy years to even out cropping and eat it within days of picking.

name: Lucombe's Seedling

origin.place: Lucombe, Pince & Co. nursery, St Thomas, Exeter, Devon

history: Raised by the Exeter nursery Lucombe, Pince & Co. and described in 1831; it was once widely grown in Devon and Cornwall under local names such as Kirton Fair and Newquay Prizetaker.

look.description: Large, angular pale yellow-green apple streaked with crimson and dotted with dark spots, on a short thick stalk.

taste.summary: Firm, juicy white flesh with a pleasant subacid flavour and a spicy note; used both for the kitchen and for eating.

pollination.notes: National Fruit Collection blossom dates are mid-season (about group 3).

climate.best_climates: The mild, moist south-west of England, where it was popular.

grow_notes: A West Country heritage apple worth growing in Devon and Cornwall orchards. The tree is modest in vigour, so a more vigorous rootstock suits it.

name: Mannington's Pearmain

origin.raised_by: Mr Turley (grew the seedling); introduced by John Mannington

history: Grew from pips in cider pomace thrown out in Mr Turley's garden at Uckfield around 1770, and was put on the market by John Mannington in 1847.

look.description: Roundish greenish-yellow to golden apple with a brownish-red or pinkish flush and some russet.

taste.summary: Firm, fine-grained, moderately juicy flesh with a rich, sweet, subtly aromatic flavour and a hint of nuttiness.

tree.notes: Reasonably vigorous and a reliable cropper; National Fruit Collection trees have a drooping habit.

pollination.notes: National Fruit Collection blossom dates are mid-late (about group 4).

climate.best_climates: South-east England, where it arose; also grown in coastal British Columbia.
climate.poor_climates: No documented performance in hot or very cold regions.

grow_notes: A Sussex late keeper for heritage collections. Pick in mid October and store until the new year, when the flavour is richest.

name: Medina

origin.place: New York State Agricultural Experiment Station, Geneva, New York

history: Raised in 1911 by Richard Wellington at the Geneva station in New York and introduced in 1922-23 as a larger, later Delicious-type apple.

look.description: Ribbed, flattish golden-yellow apple with orange-red to red mottling and streaks.

taste.summary: Tender, fairly coarse yellowish flesh, sweet with low acidity and a pronounced perfumed aroma in the Delicious style.

pollination.notes: National Fruit Collection blossom dates are mid-season (about group 3-4).

climate.best_climates: Bred for western New York; warm-summer, cold-winter climates.
climate.poor_climates: No documented performance outside the north-eastern US and English trials.

grow_notes: A Delicious-style keeper of mainly historical interest. Pick in mid October and store for early winter eating.
